objective: Troubleshoot configuration with istioctl analyze, istioctl x describe and validation messages, and common conflicts between VirtualServices and DestinationRules
secondaryObjectives: Troubleshoot the mesh control plane: istiod health, configuration distribution status (istioctl proxy-status), revision mismatches and injection failures
Troubleshoot the mesh data plane: Envoy access logs and response flags, istioctl proxy-config for listeners, routes, clusters and endpoints, and debugging mTLS and policy denials

sources.cite: Linux Foundation Education, Istio Certified Associate (ICA) certification page
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the certification body's page, found by WebSearch. Confirms the exam domains and weights: Installation, Upgrade and Configuration 20%, Traffic Management 35%, Securing Workloads 25%, Troubleshooting 20%. The objective wording is the course seed's.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: istioctl analyze reports IST0101 when a resource references another that does not exist; fix the reference and apply the configuration again.

sources.cite: Istio documentation, Debugging Envoy and Istiod (v1.6)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: istioctl proxy-status: SYNCED means Envoy acknowledged istiod's last configuration, STALE means istiod sent an update that was not acknowledged; istioctl proxy-config cluster shows a proxy's clusters.

The company, the mesh, the services and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are on call for the mesh at Tamberly Books, a fictional online bookstore. Twenty minutes ago a developer shifted 20% of reviews traffic to a v2 canary. Since then 20% of product pages show 503 errors.
handover: The change: a VirtualService routes 20% of reviews to subset v2.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

effects.output: Error [IST0101] (VirtualService bookstore/reviews) Referenced host+subset in destinationrule not found: "reviews+v2"

effects.finding: The VirtualService sends 20% to subset v2, but the reviews DestinationRule defines only v1. Envoy has no cluster for v2, so those requests fail with response flag NC.

effects.finding: Two proxies are STALE: istiod sent them configuration they have not acknowledged since its restarts. istiod's log shows it hitting its memory limit.

options.label: The missing v2 subset found by analyze and defined, istiod's memory fixed and every proxy SYNCED, and the TLS override corrected from the proxy config

then.log: Check-in 2: the restarts take capacity down during the evening peak; 503s continue at 20% on top of slow pages.
Check-in 3: during the reinstall, autoscaled Pods start without certificates and fail every mTLS call.
Check-in 4: with ratings outside the mesh, STRICT clients cannot reach it at all; every product page loses its ratings.

effects.log: Check-in 2: some proxies still behave differently.

subsetPrompt.title: Route to a subset that doesn't exist
subsetPrompt.context: The DestinationRule has no v2 subset. The v2 Pods are labeled version=v2.

choices.label: Add subset v2 (version: v2) to the DestinationRule, apply it before relying on the route, and rerun istioctl analyze until clean

effects.log: Subset v2 exists; analyze is clean; 503s stop.

choices.feedback: A route to a subset needs the DestinationRule to define it first; analyze confirms the conflict is gone.

choices.label: Roll the VirtualService back to 100% v1 and leave the canary for tomorrow
choices.feedback: 503s stop, but the canary is canceled and nobody fixed the missing subset.

choices.label: Restart every Pod in the namespace to clear Envoy's state
choices.feedback: Restarts don't create a missing subset; the 503s continue, now with a capacity dip.

stalePrompt.title: STALE proxies
stalePrompt.context: istiod is hitting its memory limit and restarting; two proxies never acknowledged the latest config.

choices.label: Raise istiod's memory request and limit and run two replicas, then confirm every proxy is SYNCED in istioctl proxy-status

effects.log: istiod is stable; every proxy is SYNCED.

choices.feedback: STALE means istiod sent configuration the proxy has not acknowledged; with istiod restarting at its memory limit, fix istiod and verify every proxy is SYNCED.

choices.label: Restart the two STALE Pods so they reconnect

effects.log: The two Pods restart and sync.

choices.feedback: They sync, but istiod will run out of memory again and leave more proxies stale.

choices.label: Delete the istiod Deployment and reinstall it from scratch

effects.log: istiod is deleted for a reinstall.

choices.feedback: With istiod gone, no new Pod gets a certificate or configuration; anything that restarts cannot join the mesh.

tlsPrompt.title: ratings fails with UF
tlsPrompt.context: productpage to ratings fails with 503 and flag UF. The namespace is STRICT; ratings' DestinationRule sets tls mode DISABLE from an old test.

choices.label: Confirm with istioctl proxy-config cluster that the client sends plaintext, then set the DestinationRule's tls mode to ISTIO_MUTUAL (or remove the override)

effects.log: The client now sends mTLS; ratings answers.

choices.feedback: A client-side DISABLE against a STRICT server fails the connection; the proxy's cluster config shows it.

choices.label: Set ratings' PeerAuthentication to PERMISSIVE
choices.feedback: It works, but ratings now accepts plaintext from anyone, and the wrong DestinationRule stays.

choices.label: Remove ratings from the mesh by disabling sidecar injection
choices.feedback: STRICT callers can no longer reach a workload without a sidecar, and ratings loses mTLS and policy.

reflection.question: Write the incident record: the three causes of the 503s and the evidence for each.

parts.label: Configuration and control plane
parts.criteria: IST0101 named the missing subset; proxy-status showed STALE proxies from an istiod memory limit.
parts.modelAnswer: analyze reported the v2 subset missing, so 20% of requests had no cluster (NC); istiod was OOM-restarting, leaving two proxies STALE.

parts.label: Data plane
parts.criteria: A UF flag on ratings; proxy-config showed the client sending plaintext due to tls DISABLE.
parts.modelAnswer: ratings calls failed with UF; the client's cluster config showed tls DISABLE against a STRICT namespace; we set ISTIO_MUTUAL.

expertPath.text: Run istioctl analyze and check proxy sync status before changing anything.
Define the v2 subset in the DestinationRule and rerun analyze.
Give istiod the resources and replicas it needs and confirm every proxy is SYNCED.
Read the client's cluster TLS settings and set ISTIO_MUTUAL.

subsetHarm.body: istioctl analyze names the conflict; restarts don't fix configuration.

scoring.modelReasoning: Read the mesh's own evidence. istioctl analyze reports conflicts such as a VirtualService routing to a subset its DestinationRule does not define (requests then fail with NC). istioctl proxy-status shows whether istiod's configuration reached each proxy; STALE points at the control plane. Envoy's response flags and istioctl proxy-config show the data plane: a client DestinationRule with tls DISABLE against a STRICT server fails with UF. Restarting Pods, deleting istiod or leaving the mesh removes evidence and capacity without fixing the cause.
